messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Renjin and loading packages
parts:
Hi Andy,
(cc'ing google group, please share questions with everyone!)

Renjin no longer supports loading packages compiled by GNU R, principally because GNU R now compiles packages to GNU R bytecode by default, for which we're taking a different approach.

We've started to set up a build cluster to automatically build CRAN packages: see http://packages.renjin.org (though it's a bit out of date)
You can also compile your own packages using the renjin-maven-plugin.

HTH,
Alex

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Renjin and loading packages
parts:
Hi Andy,
Those packages are built with the renjin-maven-plugin, the only thing we do is generate a POM file based on the DESCRIPTION file:

See for example:
http://nexus.bedatadriven.com/content/groups/public/org/renjin/cran/KernSmooth/2.23-8-SNAPSHOT/KernSmooth-2.23-8-20130217.125415-1.pom

I haven't looked yet at testthat, but I suspect the issue is with Renjin's support for the S4 type system. The code is there: most of the S4 system is actually written in R, and we've implemented the handful of "native" hooks that this code expects, but I think there are some complexities surrounding packages and S4 that I've missed. 

Generally -- I think we might be better off pulling the whole of the S4 type system out of "user space" and into the interpreter itself. It is of course very meta to implement in a language's type system in that language itself, but my sense is that it has enormous costs in turns of complexity, and also lost opportunities for optimization as the interpreter doesn't have any special knowledge about S4 classes/methods. 

But if you can find a few quick fixes to get S4 packages running that would be obviously be well worth the time in the near time!

Best,
Alex

messages.author: 3b104dc6686d0c85
messages.subject: Re: Renjin and loading packages
parts:
Actually, Hadley has recently introduced Rcpp as a dependency in many of the packages that he maintains, including testthat and roxygen2. Renjin doesn't support C++ code so I doubt that you would get a recent version of testthat to build.

If you're interested in writing R language tests for Renjin you should use the built in hamcrest package. See http://docs.renjin.org/en/latest/writing-renjin-extensions.html#using-the-hamcrest-package-to-write-unit-tests for the documentation.

Maarten-Jan
